primary_task: Research a topic on the web and return curated findings with source URLs, credibility assessment and direct quotes.

requirements.name: web_search
requirements.evidence: "You are a search specialist expert at finding and synthesizing information from the web."; "3. Search broadly first, then refine"; "Curated findings with source URLs"
requirements.basis: "web_search": "search the public web and read result snippets"

requirements.name: web_fetch (arbitrary result hosts)
requirements.evidence: "### WebFetch Deep Dive" / "Extract full content from promising results" -- a strategy section, not a numbered required step; quotes can come from search snippets.
requirements.basis: "web_fetch": "fetch a web page or unauthenticated API by URL; hosts outside the egress allow-list are refused" and "network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused"

requirements.name: web_search domain filtering (allowed_domains/blocked_domains)
requirements.evidence: "allowed_domains for trusted sources"; "blocked_domains to exclude unreliable sites"
requirements.basis: The manifest describes web_search only as "search the public web and read result snippets"; it does not say whether domain filters are supported.

notes: I read web_search as the only hard requirement and WebFetch as an optional deep-dive strategy. Other reading: if 'Extract full content from promising results' and 'Always provide direct quotes' are taken as requiring full-page fetches, web_fetch becomes hard; it works only for allow-listed hosts (GitHub, PyPI, npm, ...), so for general web research it would be BLOCKED on tool:web_fetch. Unknown: support for allowed_domains/blocked_domains in web_search.
